experiments.evidence: price ÷ full cost 1.08 (two) vs 1.07 (one); sellers’ share 65.1 % vs 64.5 %; short 0 vs 0. With two sellers per good, basics sold at 1.08× their full cost; with one, at 1.07×. Sellers kept 65.1 % vs 64.5 % of basics revenue above variable cost. The poorest decile lived at 7.02 vs 7.58.
experiments.takeaway: With two sellers per good, basics sold at 1.08× their full cost; with one seller, at 1.07×.

experiments.question: Which price rule feeds everyone?
experiments.ruleChanged: Forward-margin price with Mark-0’s guard (base) vs Primer’s adaptive price (changed): each seller asks 3 % more after a day it sold out, and 3 % less after a day with stock left.
experiments.claim: A price that reads need and the harvest pipeline feeds everyone: no one short, and no more shortage or price swing than Primer’s baseline.
experiments.evidence: short 0 (forward) vs 653,560 (Primer); daily swing 0.7 % vs 2.3 %. With the forward margin, 0 person-days were short; with Primer’s adaptive price, 653,560. Basics’ prices swung 0.7 % a day vs 2.3 %. The poorest decile lived at 7.02 vs 4.18.
experiments.takeaway: People were short on 0 person-days with the forward margin and 653,560 with Primer’s adaptive price, whose basics’ prices swung more from day to day.

experiments.question: Does more money make us richer?
experiments.ruleChanged: 24 (base) vs 48 (changed) HEARTS a day for every person. The Aven rate card is a number in R indexed to the HEARTS issued a day (HEARTS a day ÷ 24), so it doubles too. HEARTS never pay for goods.
experiments.claim: Doubling HEARTS changes only prices: real consumption of every good, and the mean living standard, within ±1 %. This holds because the Aven rate card (in R) is indexed to the HEARTS issued a day; with the card fixed in R it does not (the proof suite’s B28 reports that world).
experiments.evidence: largest change: compute -0.2 %; living standard -0.1 %; food -0.0 %, water 0.0 %, energy 0.0 %, bed -0.0 %, goods -0.0 %, spring -0.0 %, compute -0.2 %. With twice the HEARTS, food’s price in R went ×2.00, water’s ×2.00, energy’s ×2.00. What people got changed by at most 0.2 % for any good. The mean living standard changed by -0.1 %.
experiments.takeaway: With twice the HEARTS, food’s price in R went ×2 while what people got of any good changed by at most 0.2 %.

experiments.question: Does more energy make us richer?
experiments.ruleChanged: The geothermal stage and R&D on surplus energy on (base) vs both off (changed).
experiments.claim: Living standards (mean and poorest decile) end higher with surplus energy and R&D than without, and recipes get better only with it.
experiments.evidence: mean 8.33 vs 6.70; poorest decile 8.30 vs 6.69; recipes 60.9 % vs 0.0 % of the way to their physical best. With geothermal and R&D, a person used 97.23 kWh a day in the last year, 95.80 kWh were exported for accelerators and 47.52 kWh were surplus (R&D, storage, curtailed); R&D took 115,083 MWh over the run (recipes 60.9 % of the way to their physical best). Without, 55.60 kWh used, 46.96 exported, and 0.0 %. The poorest decile went from 5.03 to 8.30 with surplus energy, and from 4.27 to 6.69 without. Person-days short: 0 vs 812,803.
experiments.takeaway: With geothermal and R&D the poorest tenth went from 5.03 to 8.3 R a day; without them, from 4.27 to 6.69.

experiments.question: What stops a small village first?
experiments.ruleChanged: 1,500 blobs (base) vs 600 blobs (changed) in the same village, built for 1,500, with dome solar and no geothermal stage yet (world model 5.5). This experiment changes the population.
experiments.claim: Physics, not money, sets the limit: MIND never binds a basic while physics allows need, and fewer people on the same hex are short less.
experiments.evidence: MIND-bound basic day-goods 61 (1,500) and 28 (600); person-days short of a basic 94,643 (1,500) and 16,800 (600); days short a person 63.10 vs 28.00; short days by limit (1,500): {"water: MIND":30,"bed: not built (free land, no project)":8,"bed: MIND":31,"bed: energy":31}. With 1,500 blobs, someone was short of energy on 0 days and of water on 30. With 600, on 0 and 14 days. MIND bound a basic on 61 day-goods with 1,500 and 28 with 600. Wood was bound by demand (1,500) and demand (600).
experiments.takeaway: With 1,500 blobs, 94,643 person-days were short of a basic (63.10 days a person; someone short of energy on 0 days); with 600 in the same village, 16,800 person-days (28.00 a person; energy on 0 days). MIND bound a basic on 61 and 28 day-goods.

experiments.question: Do newcomers eat?
experiments.ruleChanged: A constant population (base) vs +2 % a year (changed), on the same fixed land. Newcomers arrive with an Aven and nothing held.
experiments.claim: Growth raises rent, not hunger: newcomers are never short, and ground rent ends higher than with a constant population.
experiments.evidence: newcomers short 0 of 64705 person-days; rent at the end 1.74e-5 (growth) vs 1.68e-5 (constant). With growth the village went from 1500 to 1606 people. Newcomers lived 64,705 person-days in their first three years and were short on 0. Ground rent went from 7.74e-5 to 1.74e-5 R a m² a day (constant population: 1.68e-5). The mean living standard ended at 8.26 vs 8.33.
experiments.takeaway: The village grew to 1606 people; newcomers were never short, and ground rent ended 1.04× the rent with a constant population.

experiments.question: Private land or City land?
experiments.ruleChanged: All land belongs to the City COOP and is leased for ground rent (base) vs land owned by people, unequally (a Pareto draw), with the rent paid to them (changed).
experiments.claim: Land that nobody can sell keeps ownership fairer: the holdings Gini ends lower with City land than with private land, and nobody is short.
experiments.evidence: Gini 0.33 (City) vs 0.34 (private); short 0 vs 58. With City land the holdings Gini ended at 0.33; with private land, at 0.34. The poorest decile lived at 8.31 vs 8.29, the top decile at 8.33 vs 8.34.
experiments.takeaway: The holdings Gini ended at 0.33 with City land and at 0.34 with private land.

experiments.question: What happens on day 1?
experiments.ruleChanged: The bootstrap on (base: each Aven’s first HEARTS go to the basics COOPs it buys from, and pools fill on day 0) vs off (changed: first HEARTS into three COOPs of the Aven’s taste).
experiments.claim: Seed the pools, and the first day feeds everyone: with the bootstrap nobody is short on day 0 or after.
experiments.evidence: bootstrap: 0.0 % short on day 0, 0 person-days in year 1; without: 0.7 % on day 0, 68,855 person-days. With the bootstrap, 0.0 % of people were short on day 0 and 0.0 % on day 1. Without it, 0.7 % and 0.7 %. Over year 1: 0 vs 68,855 person-days short.
experiments.takeaway: With the bootstrap nobody went short on day 0; without it, 1 % did.

experiments.question: Does doubling a binding physical limit raise living standards?
experiments.ruleChanged: The hot spring’s warm ponds are fixed by nature and bind every day: 2 sites (base) vs 4 (changed).
experiments.claim: Doubling the binding physical limit raises living standards: more of the good, a higher mean living standard and a higher one for the poorest decile.
experiments.evidence: spring 1.18 → 2.00 h a person a day (badge “nature” on 99.1 % of base days), mean 7.57 → 8.40, poorest decile 7.02 → 8.36; capacity per person 8.31 → 9.13. Doubling the warm ponds took spring time from 1.18 to 2.00 hours a person a day, and its price from 3.66 to 0.32 R. The mean living standard went from 7.57 to 8.40 (10.9 %), the poorest decile’s from 7.02 to 8.36.
experiments.takeaway: Doubling the warm ponds took spring time from 1.18 to 2 hours a person a day and changed the mean living standard by 10.9 %.

experiments.question: What does the tower add, and what does it cost?
experiments.ruleChanged: The village without the Tower180 (base: one more Dome120 of utilities and community halls in the centre hex) vs with it (changed), at its real cost: the tower’s shell, floors and equipment on the founding bill, its beds, its solar cells, its halls’ upkeep, climate and heat.

Beds 1,740 vs 1,848; solar 60.02 vs 63.37 GWh a year. Electricity made 124.63 vs 134.26 kWh a person a day; exported 61.68 vs 55.63. Imports €46,751,614 vs €73,159,909 a year (materials €45,894,088 vs €72,097,007). Person-days short 0 vs 1,341; mean living standard 8.33 vs 8.08, poorest tenth 8.30 vs 8.08.
experiments.takeaway: The tower adds 108 beds and 3.35 GWh of solar a year for €250 M more at the founding; the mean living standard changes by -3.0 %.

experiments.ruleChanged: Electricity is the village’s only export (base) vs the MaiaCity COOP also buying Aven service from avenCEO in MIND and selling it abroad for euros (changed): at a sourced market price for an accelerator-hour (€2), bounded by a small provider’s demand (1,024 accelerators at 55 % use), only while the bank is behind and while an accelerator-hour abroad earns more than its electricity and its accelerator cost in euros.

Aven help 24.00 vs 24.00 h a person a day, work 7.93 vs 7.48 h; person-days short 0 vs 0; mean living standard 8.32 vs 8.32, poorest tenth 7.95 vs 7.99.

experiments.question: Through a drought, a dark winter, two failing COOPs and a failing well, does everyone keep the basics, and does every decile recover within two years?
experiments.ruleChanged: No shocks (base) vs five scheduled shocks (changed): a drought (rain −50 %, summer of year 2), a dark winter (sun −60 %, winter of year 3), two COOPs’ output to 10 % for a year (WEST, the West settlement COOP selling beds, and GOODS-A, year 5), and the geothermal well down for 90 days (winter of year 6).
experiments.claim: Nobody is short in any shock, and every decile is back within two years (P3 holds with the shocks excused for two years).
experiments.evidence: short 174,623 person-days ({"water: MIND":45,"bed: not built (free land, no project)":30,"bed: energy":45,"bed: MIND":45}); P3 fails (worst fall outside the windows 16.2 %; failing: holdings tenth 1, holdings tenth 2, holdings tenth 3, holdings tenth 4, holdings tenth 5, holdings tenth 6, holdings tenth 7, holdings tenth 8, holdings tenth 9, holdings tenth 10, aven tenth 1, aven tenth 2, aven tenth 3, aven tenth 4, aven tenth 5, aven tenth 6, aven tenth 7, aven tenth 8, aven tenth 9, aven tenth 10). Through the shocks, 174,623 person-days were short of a basic (0 without shocks). The largest fall of any decile outside the two-year recovery windows was 16.2 % (23.4 % without). The mean living standard ended at 8.33 vs 8.33. There were 3 receiverships vs 1.
experiments.takeaway: Through the five shocks people were short on 174,623 person-days, and not every tenth was back within two years.
